### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **37** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**41** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f7960893cd4851472351b841d34fbe5aded345b2`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f7960893cd4851472351b841d34fbe5aded345b2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9d7e023eac86221f49f85c128bf61026ad2993b8` — the merge of head `08d51040cfd8df00f013717fc9191c7d5e127354` into base `f7960893cd4851472351b841d34fbe5aded345b2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9d7e023eac86221f49f85c128bf61026ad2993b8 && git checkout 9d7e023eac86221f49f85c128bf61026ad2993b8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f7960893cd4851472351b841d34fbe5aded345b2 08d51040cfd8df00f013717fc9191c7d5e127354 && git checkout -B drift-repro f7960893cd4851472351b841d34fbe5aded345b2 && git merge --no-ff 08d51040cfd8df00f013717fc9191c7d5e127354

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f7960893cd4851472351b841d34fbe5aded345b2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f7960893cd4851472351b841d34fbe5aded345b2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### L1 review (#34728) · 2026-11-18T06:55Z

L1: REWORK (one must-fix, in `PreferenceResolver.effectiveFor`)
Head-sha: 68019537156d21f61065afcac1df87ef6958dcf5

This is the first L1 on this PR. I read the full diff against the merge-base `0e46840fca`: 45 files, +2446/−36. I also read ruling 6968686390 (route A) as amended by 6969143776 (the policy shape), the claim 6969181499, and the os-dev report 6970102872 (final round).

**Against the rulings.**
- **Member policy.** `member_default` grants `sys_notification_preference` read, create and edit, with no `allowDelete`. The new policy `sys_notification_preference_self` is `operation: 'all'`, `using: user_id == current_user.id`, `check: user_id == current_user.id`, `positions: ['org_member']`. That is exactly ruling 6969143776's shape, and the comment beside it says why each key is load-bearing.
- **The readings pinned.** The integration suite drives the real write gate and the real caller resolver:
  - a member's create with `user_id` omitted, null, empty or another person's is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, with nothing stored;
  - moving a self-created row, or a row an administrator wrote in their name, to another person or to empty is refused `403`, and the owner is kept;
  - the default row and another member's row answer `404`;
  - delete is refused;
  - the administrator lists every row, writes the default, and edits another person's row;
  - a member's own mute affects only them on the next emit, and a mandatory topic still goes through.
  The report records the `check` and `positions` ablations as red.
- **The read route.** `GET /api/v1/messaging/me/preferences` is new and caller-scoped:
  - it takes no `user` parameter, and any query parameter is refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`;
  - the order is caller, held sign-in `403`, then anonymous `401`, the `preference-options` posture;
  - it is computed by `PreferenceResolver.effectiveFor` with the same `resolveRow`, `resolveDigest`, `resolveQuietHours` and `isMandatory` that `filter` uses, and a pin asserts every cell equals what `filter` decides;
  - `preference-options` is not extended, and there is no reset or delete door.
  This matches ruling 6968686390's route A.
- **What leaves the door.** Rows of other users are dropped in `indexRows` before anything is computed, and only the caller's own row ids are answered (`ownRowId`). The pin "nothing of another person or another organization leaves the door" holds that. A missing organization reads no row.

**Shape and scope.**
- `Fixes #34728` is on the first card line, with no closing keyword next to another open card. `Clause-②: yes` (a new public route) and `Metadata-protocol: none` match the diff.
- The out-of-surface paths are declared in the Acceptance notes with reasons, and I accept each:
  - the i18n locales (the `mobileApp` precedent);
  - the plugin-security devDependency on `service-messaging`, its vitest source alias and the lockfile, with no cycle (service-messaging does not depend on plugin-security);
  - `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` (the gate requires a new route module to be declared);
  - the two census and count pins.
- The overlap-check conflict with #34223 is in that PR's own regions of `connect-agent-both-halves-wire.pin.test.ts`, not in this PR's added hunk, and I accept the reading.
- The route ledger row is `server-only`, and the conformance test mounts the new registrar. Not governed (0 of 45 paths), 2,482 changed lines, under the threshold.
- Owed beyond L1: the contract review for `Clause-②: yes` plus the permission face (the body's own line).

**Changeset.** `.changeset/34728-notification-settings.md` is new and edits no changeset on main. It bumps `service-messaging`, `plugin-security`, `platform-objects`, `app-shell` and `i18n` as `patch`. I checked its sentences against the diff:
- The page lives under Inbox and appears only when the messaging service runs (`requiresService: 'messaging'`).
- The read's posture (`401`, held sign-in `403`, any parameter `400`, an unreadable source `500`) matches the route.
- The policy's row scope, write check and `org_member`, plus the refusal list, match the policy and its pins.
- "Administrators are unchanged" matches the policy and its pins.
- The digest and quiet-hours paragraph matches `generalWrite` (it creates or edits the caller's own `(*, *)` row) and the page hint.
- One sentence is undercut by M1: "a source it cannot read is `500` … never a partial … answer".

**CI at this head**, read from check-runs (73): 62 success, 11 skipped, none failed, none in progress.

#### Must-fix
- **M1. `effectiveFor` reads the whole organization's preference rows with `limit: 10000`, so a large organization gets a silently partial answer about the caller.**
  - The read is `data.find('sys_notification_preference', { where: { organization_id }, limit: 10000 })` under the system context, with no order. It then keeps only the caller's rows and the default rows in memory.
  - Failure scenario: an organization holds more than 10,000 preference rows (about 700 people with 15 rows each). Some or all of the caller's own rows fall outside the page. Their cells then answer `source: 'default'` or `'builtin'` with no `ownRowId`, and the door returns `200`. That breaks its own promise ("never a partial … answer") and the changeset's.
  - The page then acts on it. `cellWrite` and `generalWrite` take the `create` branch for a cell that already has a row, which stores a second `(user, topic, channel)` row. `indexRows` keeps whichever of the two it sees last, for this door and for `emit`.
  - Fix: read only what the answer needs, which is the caller's rows and the default rows. For example, use equality queries on `user_id` (the caller's id, and each global-default spelling `isGlobalDefaultUser` accepts) under the `organization_id` term, as `loadRows` uses equality queries per topic. Also treat a read that fills its limit as a fault (`500`) rather than an answer.
  - Pin both with one case: an organization whose rows exceed the page, where the caller's row still comes back as `own` with its id. If the cap stays, the fault arm needs its own pin.
  - I'll read that delta alone.

#### Should-fix
None.

#### Notes
- **N1.** `filter`'s `loadRows` for `emit` has a per-topic cap of the same size: two equality queries, each `limit: 10000`. That is older than this PR and not in its surface. If you agree it matters at that scale, a card for the emit side would keep the two readings honest together.
- **N2.** `generalWrite` copies the effective general on/off into the caller's new `(*, *)` row, even when that value came from the organization default. From then on the organization's later change to the general default no longer reaches them. The changeset and the page hint say this ("applies in place of the organization's defaults"), so I accept it as disclosed.
- **N3.** #35123 (the resolver's fall-through on a stored `none` digest or empty quiet hours) is filed, and the page offers only values that take effect. I agree that the resolver change is not this card's.
- **Landing.** Owed: M1 and its delta L1, then the contract review (`Clause-②: yes` and the permission face).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `68019537156d21f61065afcac1df87ef6958dcf5`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #34728 (body and every comment, rulings 6968686390 and 6969143776 and os-dev-report 6968930571 included), the PR #35122 body, its 46-file list and the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff (`writeCheckPolicies` and the layered RLS filter, `builtin-positions.ts`, `mapMembershipRole`, `heldPositionNames`, `PreferenceResolver.filter`, `readPreferenceOptions`) was read at the head to judge the diff. It was not reviewed. Gate verdicts: 73 check-runs, 62 `success`, 11 `skipped` by their own `if:`, none failed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **New accept set: `GET /api/v1/messaging/me/preferences` (`my-preferences-routes.ts`). Right.**
  - It refuses in this order: caller resolution (an authz-store or API-key-lifecycle refusal is relayed with its own status, anything else is `500`), then a held sign-in `403`, then anonymous `401`, then any query parameter `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. The closed query set is empty and there is no `user` parameter. This matches the posture of `preference-options`.
  - It answers only the caller's effective matrix. `ownRowId` is looked up on the caller's own index key alone, the rows of other people are dropped in `indexRows`, and the organization's default reaches the caller only as `source: 'default'` plus the effective value. That is the ruled answer (6968686390, "What is ruled", first bullet).
  - The topic list comes from `readPreferenceOptions`, the same read `GET /api/v1/messaging/preference-options` already answers to any signed-in member, so the stored-topic names add no new exposure.
  - The read is bounded by `organization_id = context.tenantId`, the same organization source the options door uses. No row or value outside the caller's own effective preference leaves. See F2 for the cost of how it reads.
- **New public surface: `member_default` grants `sys_notification_preference` read, create and edit, with no delete. Right in its bits, wrong in its reach (F1).** The grant has no `positions` domain, so it reaches every principal that holds the `everyone` anchor. Only its row-scope policy is limited to `org_member`.
- **New policy `sys_notification_preference_self`: `operation: 'all'`, `using` and `check` both `user_id == current_user.id`, `positions: ['org_member']`. Right as ruled, and right in how it composes, for `org_member`.**
  - In `writeCheckPolicies` case 1, a declared `check` puts the `owner_only_writes` floor out of the post-image check. A member therefore cannot move a row they created to another person or to the empty user. The pre-image still takes the OR of the floor and the self `using`, so a member can edit a row an administrator wrote in their name, and the check keeps it theirs.
  - This is the first shipped policy that declares a `check`. Ablations on the head blob `f2444a76` show each of the two added keys is load-bearing.
  - The ruling's unmeasured note still applies: a member who also holds another set that widens writes on this object is narrowed to their own rows by case 1. No shipped set does this today.
- **`PreferenceResolver.effectiveFor` and `MessagingService.effectivePreferencesFor`: new public methods on exported classes, additive. Right.**
  - `filter()` behaves the same after the refactor. `indexRows` is the old inline loop with `id`, `user`, `topic` and `channel` added. `resolveDigest` and `resolveQuietHours` now return the row, and every call site in `filter()` reads `.digest`, `.quietHours` or `.quietHours.tz` from it.
  - `effectiveFor` does not fail open, which matches the door's posture.
  - Its return types are not re-exported from the package index (F5).
- **Account app nav entry `nav_account_notification_settings`. Right.** It has `componentRef: 'account:notification_settings'` and `requiresService: 'messaging'`, it is in all 11 translation packs, and the CLI nav-count pin moves from 14 to 15.
- **The route ledger row (`server-only`) and the `check-route-envelope` MODULES declaration (0/0/0, shared `sendOk`/`sendError`/`sendServerFault`). Right.**
- **Console: `NotificationSettingsPage`, `myPreferences.ts`, the `@object-ui/i18n` `notificationSettings` namespace. Right.**
  - The page reads through the host's authenticated `apiFetch` and writes through `useAdapter()` as the person. A mandatory topic writes nothing.
  - It offers only digest and quiet-hours values that take effect.
  - The census entry in `affordanceGrantMap-12082` marks these writes `outOfFamily`.
- **The `plugin-security` devDependency on `service-messaging`, its vitest alias and the lockfile. Right.** They are test-only, and `Validate Package Dependencies` is green.

### ② Semver level

These are the five packages whose published source the diff moves. The CLI pin and the scripts publish nothing.
